name: Paris-Brest
description: A ring of choux pastry split and filled with hazelnut praline mousseline cream, dusted with icing sugar.
ingredients: a pinch of cracked black peppercorns
a handful of fresh parsley, chopped
a generous spoonful of crème fraîche
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with extra-virgin olive oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the puff pastry and fresh thyme until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the Gruyère cheese with the dry red wine until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 35 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with chives or a dusting of cognac.
Slice or portion into servings and serve.
tips: This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
